title: Instructions a literal reader can follow
statement: Write instructions a literal reader can follow: verbs match actions, units match what can be selected, and each fill-in frame stays grammatical and sensible for every possible value.
detail: A review of a Grade 5 course found a prompt that kept a selection verb on a free-writing box, so a student would look for four sentences to pick, and an item that said to tap two sentences when each tappable unit was a whole paragraph (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-19-R2.md`). An outside review of a Grade 3 lesson found a fill-in frame that broke grammar ('has a enchanting'); it was rewritten so it stays grammatical whichever word fills the blank (`grade3-reading/artifacts/baseline-submission/CHANGES-FOR-REVIEW-L4-2026-08-31.md`).
against: No standing script does the substitution yet; the checklist runs it as an agent's sweep (`grade3-reading/artifacts/AlphaRead-QC-Checklist-v2-2026-09-04.md`, line 49). The shorthand "a(n) _____" is not an error in itself: it should resolve to the right article (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/closed_ended_evaluation.txt`, line 250).
